#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Airline-passenger data-quality & comparison analysis.
-----------------------------------------------------
- Reads the synthetic Parquet (local / input).
- Reads the public historical CSV downloaded via Runtime MCP.
- Computes summary statistics for both.
- Produces a comparison bar chart (PNG).
- Writes RESULT.json, REPORT.md, and delivery_manifest.json.

Quality reference guidance (from dataset-quality-review skill):
  - Synthetic observations and independently obtained public records
    have different evidential roles, even when their columns look alike.
  - Retain calculation precision in machine-readable results.
  - Apply presentation rounding separately, and state comparison limits
    when coverage, units or populations differ.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# ── Paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PARQUET_PATH = "/workspace/input/data/0/synthetic-airline.parquet"
PUBLIC_CSV_PATH = "/workspace/downloads/8cb51be753a718d9be5d76d7e238cc224792754676adc21faa59e954b0201621.txt"
PUBLIC_SOURCE_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jbrownlee/Datasets/refs/heads/master/airline-passengers.csv"
PUBLIC_SHA256 = "8cb51be753a718d9be5d76d7e238cc224792754676adc21faa59e954b0201621"
PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN = "Passengers"
DOWNLOADED_FILE = os.path.basename(PUBLIC_CSV_PATH)

OUT_DIR = "/workspace/airline-comparison"

# ── 1. Load synthetic (local) data ────────────────────────────────────
local_df = pd.read_parquet(PARQUET_PATH)
local_rows = int(len(local_df))
local_total = int(local_df["passengers"].sum())
local_mean = float(local_df["passengers"].mean())

print(f"[LOCAL] rows={local_rows}  total={local_total}  mean={local_mean!r}")
print(f"[LOCAL] data:\n{local_df.to_string()}")

# ── 2. Load public historical data ────────────────────────────────────
public_df = pd.read_csv(PUBLIC_CSV_PATH)
public_values = public_df[PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN]
public_rows = int(len(public_values))
public_total = int(public_values.sum())
public_mean = float(public_values.mean())

print(f"\n[PUBLIC] rows={public_rows}  total={public_total}  mean={public_mean!r}")
print(f"[PUBLIC] column='{PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN}'  dtype={public_values.dtype}")
print(f"[PUBLIC] head:\n{public_df.head().to_string()}")

# ── 3. Verify SHA-256 of downloaded file ──────────────────────────────
sha = hashlib.sha256()
with open(PUBLIC_CSV_PATH, "rb") as f:
    for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(8192), b""):
        sha.update(chunk)
computed_sha = sha.hexdigest()
assert computed_sha == PUBLIC_SHA256, f"SHA mismatch: {computed_sha} != {PUBLIC_SHA256}"
print(f"\n[VERIFY] SHA-256 OK: {computed_sha}")

# ── 4. Comparison metrics ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The synthetic data has 3 rows matching the first 3 months of the public
# series (1949-01, 1949-02, 1949-03).  We compare the full public series
# against the synthetic sample as instructed.
diff_total = local_total - public_total
diff_mean = local_mean - public_mean
overlap_public = public_df.head(local_rows)
overlap_values = overlap_public[PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN]
overlap_total = int(overlap_values.sum())
overlap_mean = float(overlap_values.mean())
exact_match = (local_df["passengers"].values == overlap_values.values).all()

print(f"\n[COMPARE] synthetic_total={local_total}  public_total={public_total}  diff={diff_total}")
print(f"[COMPARE] synthetic_mean={local_mean!r}  public_mean={public_mean!r}")
print(f"[COMPARE] first-{local_rows} public rows total={overlap_total}  mean={overlap_mean!r}")
print(f"[COMPARE] exact match on overlapping months: {exact_match}")

# ── 5. Chart ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

# Left: full public time series with synthetic overlay
months_str = public_df["Month"].values
x = np.arange(len(months_str))
axes[0].plot(x, public_values.values, color="steelblue", linewidth=1.2,
             label=f"Public historical ({PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN})")
# Mark the 3 synthetic months on the public timeline
local_x = np.arange(local_rows)
axes[0].scatter(local_x, local_df["passengers"].values, color="coral",
                s=80, zorder=5, edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.8,
                label="Synthetic local (Jan–Mar 1949)")
axes[0].set_xticks(x[::12])
axes[0].set_xticklabels([m[:4] for m in months_str[::12]], rotation=45, fontsize=8)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Year")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Passengers")
axes[0].set_title("Monthly Airline Passengers: Public vs Synthetic")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Right: summary bar comparison
categories = ["Synthetic\nLocal (3 mo)", "Public\nHistorical (144 mo)",
              "Public first 3\n(overlap window)"]
totals = [local_total, public_total, overlap_total]
means = [local_mean, public_mean, overlap_mean]
colors = ["#FF7F50", "#4682B4", "#87CEEB"]

ax1 = axes[1]
bars = ax1.bar(categories, totals, color=colors, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.5)
for bar, t, m in zip(bars, totals, means):
    ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 100,
             f"total={t}\nmean={m:.1f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)
ax1.set_ylabel("Passenger Total")
ax1.set_title("Totals & Means Comparison")
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", alpha=0.3)

fig.suptitle("Airline Passenger Data-Quality Comparison\n(Synthetic Local vs Public Historical)",
             fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.93])
chart_path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "comparison_chart.png")
fig.savefig(chart_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)
print(f"\n[CHART] saved: {chart_path}")

# ── 6. RESULT JSON ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
result = {
    "local_rows": local_rows,
    "local_total": local_total,
    "local_mean": local_mean,
    "public_rows": public_rows,
    "public_total": public_total,
    "public_source_url": PUBLIC_SOURCE_URL,
    "public_sha256": PUBLIC_SHA256,
    "public_value_column": PUBLIC_VALUE_COLUMN,
    "downloaded_file": DOWNLOADED_FILE,
}
result_path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "RESULT.json")
with open(result_path, "w") as f:
    json.dump(result, f, indent=2)
print(f"\n[RESULT] saved: {result_path}")
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
